proof_spine: Invoke the reserved kernel theorem to store its unique reduced-fraction existential.
Eliminate the existential and reuse both canonical body facts.

blocks.intent: Expose and consume the kernel-owned canonical rational representation.

attempts.candidate:
have q Q
by thm rational_has_unique_reduced_fraction(q)
attempts.verifier_evidence: release runner reported: by thm: theorem `rational_has_unique_reduced_fraction` is not defined
attempts.failure_mechanism: The reduced-fraction fact existed only as an automatic existential rule and a trusted std/basics wrapper; no reserved theorem name dispatched to it.
attempts.diagnosis: Add a bare reserved theorem handler that constructs the canonical existential and verifies it through the existing rule.
attempts.next_change: Reserve the name, accept one argument, construct integer/positive-natural witnesses with gcd 1, and store only after verification.

attempts.candidate:
have q Q
by thm rational_has_unique_reduced_fraction(q)
obtain p, d from exist! p Z, d N+ st {q = p / d, gcd(p, d) = 1}
q = p / d
gcd(p, d) = 1
attempts.verifier_evidence: target/release/litex -compact -isolated -runner -f examples/01_proof_patterns/rational_reduced_fraction_builtin_theorem.lit: exit 0, top-level ok=true; the nested verification cites `exist!: unique rational reduced fraction with positive denominator`.
attempts.diagnosis: The named surface and the direct existential now share one checked mathematical rule, and elimination exposes the expected numerator, denominator, ratio, and gcd facts.
attempts.next_change: Keep non-Q, arity, qualification, malformed-gcd, and no-leak cases in Rust regression coverage.

blocks.accepted_litex:

gcd(p, d) = 1
blocks.reusable_lesson: A named builtin theorem can expose a stable public constructor without adding trust when it constructs a canonical fact and delegates truth verification to an existing kernel rule.
